Subject: Quick recap & follow-ups — deployment mode and sizing clarifications

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks to help us produce an accurate Dedicated capacity proposal and (if needed) a Private/VPC option: 

Summary (what I heard)
- Primary use case: customer-facing conversational assistant + long-form summarization for uploaded docs.
- Concern: regulated data may require network isolation; procurement will push on this.
- Preference: leaning Dedicated for predictable throughput but evaluating Private VPC if compliance requires it.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm these?):
1) Peak TPS target (sustained 15m window) and expected burst factor (x): what should we size to?
2) Average / median token lengths and percent of long-context requests (>=1024 tokens). Example: short chat vs long summarization mix.
3) 99th percentile latency SLO target (ms) for user-facing requests.
4) Any hard redirects: must-have GPUs (e.g., H100 preferred), or budget constraints pushing towards A100 + quantization?
5) Timeline & procurement cadence: target PoC start date and any required procurement steps (PO, security questionnaire).

Next steps from Redwood
- I'll put together a short sizing matrix (GPU mix options + ballpark monthly cost) and a 2-week PoC plan covering performance and integration.
- Karthik will comment on concurrency settings and batching that match your token mix.

If you can reply with the numbers for Q1–Q4 above, we’ll have a very tight proposal ready by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks — appreciate the time.

— Mina

Thanks Mina — good recap. Answers below, and I’m looping procurement (Priya) on the thread so they see the ask about VPC/private.

Answers:
1) Peak TPS: planning for 30 TPS sustained in a 15-minute window with 2x burst capacity for traffic spikes.
2) Token mix (rough): ~80% short interactions (<=128 tokens total), ~15% medium (256–512), ~5% long-form (512–2048) for summarization jobs. Average tokens per request ~120–150. Max context used for long jobs: 4096 tokens.
3) Latency SLO: 99th <= 250ms for short interactions; can accept higher (up to ~1s) for long summarization jobs if batched.
4) GPU preference: we prefer H100 if budget allows (better perf for our long-context models). If cost is constrained, A100+int8/4-bit quantization is acceptable for the first phase.
5) Timeline: procurement wants vendor risk review (SOC2 evidence) and an RFP response — target PoC kickoff in mid-November (week of Nov 16). Budget: aiming for <$25k/month in committed spend for the pilot if possible.

Attached is our RFP skeleton and a short network/security checklist — procurement will add more.

–Samir

Subject: Re: Quick recap & follow-ups — deployment mode and sizing clarifications

Samir / Priya — thanks for the detail. Below are two practical Dedicated sizing options for the token mix and 30 TPS peak you described, plus tradeoffs for Private VPC: 

Option A — High-performance (preferred if H100 available)
- Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA H100 80GB nodes in a small dedicated pool; autoscale + 1 hot spare.
- Concurrency: set per-GPU concurrency to ~12–16 in the runtime to allow low tail latency for short requests while preserving KV cache for long sessions.
- Batching: continuous batching configured with 15–30ms window for short chats, larger 200–500ms batch windows for long summaries to reduce cost.
- Expected steady-state: comfortably handle 30 TPS with headroom for 2x bursts; long jobs scheduled on isolated queue to avoid tail latency impact.
- Pros: best latency for mixed token workloads, fewer nodes to manage.
- Cons: H100 unit cost higher.

Option B — Cost-conscious (A100 + quantization)
- Hardware: 3–4 x A100 80GB nodes with int8/4-bit quantization for encoder/decoder where acceptable.
- Concurrency: per-GPU concurrency ~20 (higher due to quantized lower-memory usage), but expect slightly higher 99p latency on some long requests.
- Batching: larger batching windows for summarization jobs; consider dedicated batch workers.
- Pros: lower unit-cost, more granular scaling.
- Cons: slightly higher tail latency and quantization may impact a small fraction of generation quality.

Private VPC notes:
- Network isolation adds ~2–3 days onboarding and a small ops surcharge (we'll call out specifics).
- VPC adds minimal latency overhead but gives procurement/infosec the controls they need.

PoC recommendation & next steps:
1) Run a 2-week PoC on Option A (H100) if budget allows — validate latency and long-job isolation. If budget prohibits, run PoC on Option B with a 2-week quality check.
2) Redwood to provide: capacity worksheet (attached), a short SOC2 evidence packet, and an estimated committed pricing sheet (month-to-month vs 12-month).
3) Samir/Priya: confirm peak TPS (30 ok?), confirm PoC target start week (Nov 16?) and share any RFP deadlines.

I attached our capacity worksheet and a brief diagram showing GPU allocation patterns for short vs long workloads. I’ll follow with a concise pricing ballpark after Mina and I align on the PoC flavor.

— Karthik
